title: Dutch Nationwide 24-Hour Transport Strike Halts Trains, Buses and Trams Over Welfare Cuts Tied to NATO Spending Pledge
detail: Unions FNV, CNV and VCP staged a 24-hour nationwide strike on September 9, 2026 that halted nearly all trains, buses, trams and metros across the Netherlands, including international rail services to Belgium, Germany, France and the UK. The strike targeted the cabinet's plan to cut up to €6.5 billion a year in welfare spending — chiefly by shortening unemployment benefits and scaling back disability coverage — to help finance the country's higher defense outlays under NATO's spending pledge. It went ahead despite a September 1 cabinet concession dropping plans to accelerate the state pension age increase and offering €1.5 billion to offset inflation; unions and the opposition Pro party said the offer did not go far enough, since the core unemployment and disability cuts remained. The government, a centre-right minority coalition of D66, VVD and CDA that needs opposition votes to pass its budget, is due to present that budget on September 15, keeping the standoff between social-welfare protection and defense-spending commitments unresolved heading into the vote.

media.caption: Nationwide 24-hour Dutch public transport strike over welfare cuts tied to higher NATO defense spending
